sn38.1:1.1: Situated near Nāḷandā north of Rājagaha, this village is associated with Sāriputta; the commentary says it was his home town. He speaks there twice with the wanderer Sāmaṇḍakāni ([an10.65](), [an10.66]()), and it was the site of his passing ([sn47.13]()).
sn38.1:1.2: Found only in this chapter, his name means “eater of black plums”, perhaps as an ascetic diet (cf. [mn12:52.1]()). With the exception of the final discourse, all the discourses of this chapter follow the same format, where Jambukhādaka asks for clarification of a central Dhamma term, making the chapter a handy guide to key vocabulary. Several of the terms are found in dependent origination; for explanations of these see [sn12.1]() and [sn12.2]().
sn38.1:2.1: _Nibbāna_, the going out of a flame, “quenching”.
